original_question: Given a polynomial Diophantine equation P(x1, ..., xn) = 0 with integer coefficients, determine whether its set of integer solutions is a finite union of polynomial families, where a polynomial family means a subset S of Z^n for which there exist polynomials P1, ..., Pn in integer parameters u1, ..., uk such that (x1, ..., xn) belongs to S exactly when xi = Pi(u1, ..., uk) for all i.
target_in_paper: Section 2, Definition 1 and Problem 1: the formal problem of deciding whether the integer solution set of a polynomial Diophantine equation is a finite union of polynomial families. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact formal target in Section 2: it is about a polynomial Diophantine equation with integer coefficients, its integer solution set, and whether that solution set is a finite union of polynomial families in the sense of Definition 1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))
missing_details: The paper's ambient object is a polynomial Diophantine equation F=0 with F a polynomial with integer coefficients and at least one nonconstant monomial; for a fully stand-alone version, it is better to say explicitly that F is nonconstant. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))

The solution set should be named explicitly as a subset of Z^n, for example V_F(Z) = {(x_1,...,x_n) in Z^n : F(x_1,...,x_n)=0}. Section 2 defines polynomial families as subsets of Z^n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))

The quantifier in the definition of polynomial family should be explicit: there exists some finite number m of integer parameters u_1,...,u_m and polynomials f_1,...,f_n with integer coefficients such that membership in S is equivalent to the existence of integers u_1,...,u_m satisfying x_i = f_i(u_1,...,u_m) for all i. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))

To avoid a notation clash with the equation polynomial P, the parametrizing polynomials should be renamed, for example to f_1,...,f_n. This is a presentational fix, not a change of meaning. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))

Problem 1 is the unrestricted version: it imposes no extra hypotheses such as homogeneity, symmetry, cyclicity, degree bounds, or a fixed number of monomials, so the refined question should not add any such restrictions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))

Section 3 studies a broader and explicitly informal question about describing solutions in any "reasonable" way; your draft should stay with the narrower formal Problem 1 and not drift to that neighboring problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))
refined_question: Let F(x_1,...,x_n) be a nonconstant polynomial in Z[x_1,...,x_n], and let V_F(Z) = {(x_1,...,x_n) in Z^n : F(x_1,...,x_n)=0}. Determine whether V_F(Z) can be written as a finite union of polynomial families, where a polynomial family means a subset S of Z^n for which there exist an integer m >= 1 and polynomials f_1,...,f_n in Z[u_1,...,u_m] such that, for every x=(x_1,...,x_n) in Z^n, x belongs to S if and only if there exist integers u_1,...,u_m with x_i = f_i(u_1,...,u_m) for all i=1,...,n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))
justification: Section 2 is the exact match: Definition 1 gives the paper's formal meaning of "polynomial family", and Problem 1 then asks precisely whether the integer solution set of a given polynomial Diophantine equation is a finite union of such families. Section 3 immediately contrasts this with a different, looser problem of describing solutions in any "reasonable" way, so sharpening your draft means aligning it with Problem 1 rather than broadening it to Section 3. Section 7 still refers back to Problem 1 when it discusses the shortest open cases, confirming that this is the paper's official formulation of the issue your draft is aiming at. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))
